prompts.display_text: Pin a country of more than 100 million people with a temple at any stage (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country with a population above 100 million (UN World Population Prospects) and a temple at any stage (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology; UN World Population Prospects 2024
prompts.summary: Of the 15 countries with over 100 million people, 11 have a temple at some stage as of October 2026. Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia and Egypt do not. The Philippines, Mexico, Brazil and the United States have the most dedicated temples among them, while India, Indonesia, Russia and China have temples only under construction or announced.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: About 212 million; 12 dedicated temples.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: About 130 million; 14 dedicated temples.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Over 340 million people; more than 100 dedicated temples.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: About 123 million; 4 dedicated temples.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: About 116 million; 6 dedicated temples.

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: About 109 million; Kinshasa temple.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: About 230 million; Aba Nigeria Temple.

answers.name: Indonesia
answers.fact: About 283 million; Jakarta temple announced.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: About 1.45 billion; Bengaluru temple under construction.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: About 144 million; temple announced.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: About 1.4 billion; Shanghai temple announced, Hong Kong temple dedicated.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where Haitian, Papiamento, Bislama or Tok Pisin is official.
prompts.text_original: A country or territory where a creole language with a Book of Mormon edition (Haitian, Papiamento, Bislama, Tok Pisin) is official
prompts.summary: Book of Mormon text exists in creole languages including Haitian Creole (full text 1999), Tok Pisin of Papua New Guinea (2002), Bislama of Vanuatu (2004) and Papiamento (selections 1987). Papiamento is spoken in Aruba, Curacao and Bonaire.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: Haitian Creole selections came in 1983 and the full text in 1999.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: The Tok Pisin Book of Mormon appeared in 2002.

answers.name: Aruba
answers.fact: Papiamento, given selections in 1987, is official in Aruba.

answers.name: Curacao
answers.fact: Papiamento selections appeared in 1987.

answers.name: Vanuatu
answers.fact: Bislama selections came in 1985 and the full text in 2004.

answers.name: Caribbean Netherlands
answers.fact: Papiamento, given selections in 1987, kept its official status in the Caribbean Netherlands, which includes Bonaire, in 2010.

prompts.display_text: Pin a formerly communist country that Saints names as newly open to missionaries about 1991.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 26: around 1991, missionaries were newly permitted in these formerly communist countries. Pin one.
prompts.summary: As communist governments fell around 1989 to 1991, countries that had kept missionaries out began to let them in. Saints vol. 4 ch. 26 names Poland, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Slovenia and Croatia among the newly opened countries.

answers.name: Poland
answers.fact: Opened to missionaries as the Iron Curtain fell.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Named in the chapter's list of newly opened countries.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Named in the chapter's list of newly opened countries.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Named in the chapter's list of newly opened countries.

answers.name: Croatia
answers.fact: Part of the Yugoslav breakup era; named in the list.

answers.name: Slovenia
answers.fact: Part of the Yugoslav breakup era; named in the list.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country holding a place named in Isaiah's oracles against the nations (Isaiah 13-23).
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in Isaiah's oracles against the nations (Isaiah 13-23)
prompts.summary: In Isaiah 13 to 23, the prophet delivers burdens, or warnings, against the nations around Judah. They open with Babylon's fall and include Egypt, Damascus, Moab, Tyre and Sidon, and the Arabian oasis of Tema. Isaiah also names Elam and Media, and Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt (Isaiah 20:3-5).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Babylon's fall opens the oracles (Isaiah 13).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Isaiah 19 is the burden of Egypt.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Assyria took Ashdod, a Philistine city now in Israel (Isaiah 20:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Moab gets two chapters (Isaiah 15-16).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Isaiah 23 laments Tyre and Sidon.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Damascus will become a ruinous heap (Isaiah 17:1).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Elam and Media are called to attack Babylon (Isaiah 21:2).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Isaiah 14:29-31 warns all Palestina (Philistia), whose city of Gaza is in the Gaza Strip.

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Tema, the oasis of Tayma, is told to bring water (Isaiah 21:14).

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Isaiah 20:3-5 names Ethiopia (Cush), the Nile land from Syene to near Khartoum.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose Church missionary training center closed between 2019 and 2023.
prompts.text_original: Between 2019 and 2023 the Church closed several missionary training centers outside the United States as more missionaries trained at home or online. A country whose missionary training center closed in that period.
prompts.citation: Church News 2019-02-08; Newsroom (Guatemala MTC, Colombia MTC)
prompts.summary: In 2019 the Church closed its training centers in Santiago, Madrid and Santo Domingo, then Buenos Aires that July. Guatemala City followed in January 2020 and Bogota in January 2023. Missionaries from those lands now train at home, online or at the remaining centers.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: The Buenos Aires MTC closed in July 2019.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: The Santiago MTC closed in January 2019.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: The Madrid MTC closed in January 2019.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: The Bogota MTC closed in January 2023.

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: The Santo Domingo MTC closed in January 2019.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: The Guatemala City MTC closed in January 2020.
